evidence:
control.lisp:386-390
(fnn-os-error (condition)
  (fnn-err "control request refused (os-error): ~a" condition)
  (list :reason :refused
        (fnn-core 'fn-native-control-host-refusal-reason :os-error)))
while owner.lisp:1801-1806 (fnn-owner-shared-action-locked, wrapped around every fnn-owner-serialized thunk):
((or fnn-os-error serious-condition) (condition)
  ...
  (fnn-owner-stop-service-locked service +fnn-exit-fault+)
  (error condition))
fix: Tell apart an os-error or socket-error raised before any owner work (frame read: a real refusal) from one that propagated out of fnn-owner-serialized. For example, have fnn-owner-shared-action-locked wrap non-store conditions in an fnn-store-fault after it stops the service, or check (fnn-owner-service-stopping service) in these clauses and answer :fault.
reviewer: fnn-os-error is a plain error, not a subclass of fnn-store-error (io.lisp:124). fnn-config-record-observation (io.lisp:2121-2144) calls fnn-check-regular and fnn-read-regular-bounded (io.lisp:639, which opens through fnn-open and so raises fnn-os-error) inside the handler-case at admin.lisp:258. That handler catches only fnn-store-error. The os-error therefore reaches fnn-owner-shared-action-locked (owner.lisp:1801-1806), which stops the owner with +fnn-exit-fault+ and re-raises. control.lisp:386-390 then answers (:reason :refused :os-error), so the operator is told REFUSED for a node that has stopped as a FAULT. The comment at control.lisp:369-371 lists only indeterminate and fault as the cases that fence the owner. A socket-error raised inside a serialized thunk takes the same route.
scenario: A live admin request (`peer add`, `account ...`, a POST via control) reaches fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked, and fnn-config-record-observation -> fnn-read-regular-bounded fails with EMFILE or EIO, which raises fnn-os-error. The owner wrapper stops the service with exit 4 and re-raises. The control worker's os-error clause then sends the operator REFUSED plus the reason os-error, which is exit 1 and means nothing happened, try again. In fact the node has stopped as a fault. The comment at 369-371 says only indeterminate and fault fence the owner, so it misses this path. A sb-bsd-sockets:socket-error signalled inside a serialized thunk takes the same route.
title: Control reply says REFUSED (exit 1) for an OS error after the owner already stopped itself as a FAULT
